chunks: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Mani', from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The least that a visitor of Husayn (peace be upon him) acquires is that for every good deed, one million good deeds are recorded for him, and for every bad deed, only one bad deed. And how can one be compared to a million?

Then he said: O Safwan, rejoice, for verily Allah has angels who carry rods of light. When the Keepers intend to record a bad deed for the visitor of Husayn (peace be upon him), the angels say to the Keepers, 'Stop,' so they stop.
When he performs a good deed, she says to them, 'Record it.' [These are] those whom Allah will change their bad deeds into good deeds.

key_terms.يُبَدِّلُ اللّهُ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ حَسَناتٍ: Allah changes their bad deeds to good deeds

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husayn (peace be upon him) regarding the multiplication of good deeds and cancellation of bad deeds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the immense spiritual economy of Ziyarat, where good deeds are multiplied by a million and bad deeds are recorded singly, a concept rooted in the Shia understanding of divine grace (fadl) for the Ahl al-Bayt's followers. The narration highlights the active role of celestial guardians who intervene to suppress minor faults, ensuring that the visitor's record remains pristine. This mechanism fulfills the Quranic promise of divine transformation, where Allah converts the sins of the faithful into good deeds, emphasizing the unique status of Husayn's visitors in the hereafter.
